column11: Collect a $75 deposit within 24-48 hours toward a $149 project.
column12: Owner-operated tourism, wellness, recreation, photography, event, restaurant, food-truck, and visitor-service businesses in Asheville and Buncombe County, North Carolina.
column13: Owner-operated tour, wellness, photography, or event business with 1-10 employees and an active offer but a weak, missing, or hard-to-use mobile booking path.
column15: Mobile visitors cannot quickly understand the offer or take the next step.
column16: Upcoming weekend, seasonal promotion, reopening, new service, or a social profile sending traffic to a poor website.
column17: Can approve $75-$249 quickly when the page supports a current revenue-producing offer.
column19: Sell an owner-operated business a simple mobile-friendly booking or promotional page within 24 hours. It shows the main offer, click-to-call and booking/contact actions, hours, directions, FAQs, one testimonial, and social links. A hosted preview is provided after a deposit.
column20: Test immediately, but sell it as a mobile conversion page that connects to the customer’s existing booking, ordering, phone, or contact tool. Do not promise a custom booking system for $149. The visible 24-hour turnaround and local handoff are the differentiators.

column3: Same-Day Broken Website and CTA Repair
column11: Collect a $40 deposit within 24-48 hours toward a $75 same-day repair.
column12: Asheville and Buncombe County restaurants, spas, salons, tour operators, contractors, photographers, and service businesses with broken, missing, buried, or confusing website actions.
column13: An owner-operated restaurant, salon/spa, tour operator, photographer, or home-service company whose mobile site receives traffic but has a broken or confusing primary action.
column14: Owner, manager, or the person who maintains the website
column15: Customers cannot call, book, order, see a menu, or request service because a key action is broken or hard to find.
column16: A broken link, outdated menu, recent website edit, seasonal traffic, ad campaign, or customer complaint.
column17: A $40 deposit is plausible when the defect is verified and the fix avoids lost inquiries.
column19: Fix or add up to three high-value customer-action links such as call, contact, booking, ordering, menu, map, or directions; include one reasonable mobile-layout correction, link testing, and before-and-after screenshots.
column20: This is the strongest immediate-cash test because the problem is visible, easy to demonstrate, and bounded. Keep the $75 offer for link/button fixes only; quote separately when the diagnosis reveals theme, plugin, hosting, account-access, or checkout problems.

column11: Sell one $99 pack and collect at least a $50 deposit in 24-48 hours.
column12: Asheville restaurants, food trucks, retailers, tourism businesses, event vendors, wellness providers, contractors, and other owner-operated businesses without a dedicated marketer.
column13: An owner-operated food, tourism, retail, wellness, or event business with an offer launching in the next 14 days and no in-house content employee.
column15: A real promotion exists, but the owner lacks time and ready-to-post assets.
column16: Weekend event, reopening, seasonal menu, ticket deadline, slow booking period, or new service.
column17: A $50 deposit is realistic when the package supports an imminent, specific promotion.
column19: Create a rapid promotional package with AI-assisted drafting and design followed by human editing and fact-checking: social posts, matching graphics, captions, calls to action, and a short email promoting one current offer, event, reopening, seasonal special, or service.
column20: Viable as a tightly scoped “one offer, one campaign” pack. Avoid vague monthly social-media management. Require the owner to approve all facts, prices, images, trademarks, and claims before final delivery.

column11: Book one $99 session and collect payment or at least $50 deposit in 24-48 hours.
column12: Established, newly opened, or reopened Asheville/Buncombe restaurants, contractors, salons, spas, tourism operators, professional services, and local stores with incomplete or outdated profiles.
column13: A verified, single-location local service, tourism, food, or wellness business whose public profile shows inaccurate hours, missing links, weak categories, or stale photos.
column15: Customers see wrong or incomplete information at the moment they search or navigate.
column16: Reopening, relocation, new hours, new services, ownership change, holiday schedule, or customer complaints.
column17: The $99 session is credible when the prospect can see multiple factual errors and owns a verified profile.
column19: Guide a business owner through correcting inaccurate or incomplete Google Business Profile information: categories, hours, contact details, links, services, photos, description, and other owner-approved fields. Do not promise rankings, approval, or immediate publication.
column20: Sell an owner-controlled accuracy cleanup and checklist, not “ranking optimization.” Google provides the profile free, can review edits, and controls publication. A guided session avoids requesting passwords and keeps final decisions with the owner.

column11: Sell one $75 introductory package covering up to 20 responses and collect at least a $40 deposit in 24-48 hours.
column12: Asheville restaurants, hotels, vacation services, tourism businesses, salons, spas, contractors, medical/wellness offices, retailers, and other businesses receiving regular public reviews.
column13: An independent restaurant, hotel, tour operator, salon/spa, or home-service business with at least 8 recent unanswered reviews and an identifiable owner/manager.
column14: Owner, general manager, or guest-experience manager
column15: Unanswered reviews create a visible backlog and negative reviews lack a calm, owner-approved response.
column16: Recent one-to-three-star review, reopening, management change, busy season, or growing review volume.
column17: A $40-$50 deposit is credible when the backlog is public and the tone risk is clear.
column19: Draft personalized professional responses to recent unanswered reviews, including positive, neutral, and negative reviews, a reusable tone guide, and templates. The business approves every response before posting.
column20: Demand exists inside broader reputation management, but response writing alone is easy to commoditize. Keep human review, local voice, and business approval central. Change the $75 scope to 12 responses; offer up to 20 for $99 so negative or sensitive reviews receive adequate care.

column3: Simple Lead-Capture Form and Follow-Up System
column11: Collect a $75 deposit in 24-48 hours toward a $149 setup.
column12: Asheville/Buncombe contractors, home-service providers, photographers, event vendors, consultants, wellness businesses, tour operators, and small companies relying on calls, social DMs, or outdated forms.
column13: An owner-operated contractor, photographer, event vendor, tour, or non-clinical wellness business that receives inquiries but lacks a reliable mobile form and response log.
column15: Lead details arrive across calls and DMs, are incomplete, and can be lost or answered late.
column16: Missed calls, rapid growth, new advertising, busy season, or a broken/absent website form.
column17: A $75 deposit is reasonable when a missed lead could be worth more than the setup price.
column19: Build a mobile-friendly form collecting a prospect’s name, contact information, requested service, and message; connect it to email notification or a spreadsheet; add an immediate confirmation and one follow-up template; test and hand off.
column20: A strong fixed-scope offer when sold to businesses visibly relying on DMs or broken forms. Use the customer’s own Google/Jotform account and avoid collecting sensitive health, financial, identity, or payment data in the starter package.

column11: Sell one $149-$199 starter automation and collect at least a $75 deposit in 24-48 hours.
column12: Owner-operated and small Asheville/Buncombe service businesses manually processing inquiries, appointments, follow-ups, estimates, or routine administrative information.
column13: An owner-operated contractor, photographer, event vendor, tour, or appointment business using two common cloud tools and repeating the same copy/paste or notification task several times each week.
column15: A repetitive lead or appointment task consumes time and causes delay or lost information.
column16: Higher inquiry volume, missed follow-ups, new form, new calendar, or owner overload.
column17: A $75 deposit is plausible when the owner can quantify repeated work and the workflow uses existing supported integrations.
column19: Set up one clearly defined automation that removes a repetitive administrative step—for example routing a form to a spreadsheet, notifying an owner, sending a confirmation, organizing inquiries, creating reminders, or connecting two existing tools.
column20: Viable if the opening offer is one trigger, one or two actions, and existing supported tools. Avoid vague “AI automation” promises. The customer should own every account and recurring subscription, and the workflow must include failure alerts and a manual fallback.
